Q0170

“I ask the channel how it can be so clear — because…” — Zhu Xi (Reflections on Reading, no. 1)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Reflections on Reading, no. 1. Theme: learning.

Quotes / Zhu Xi / Q0170

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Reflections on Reading, no. 1 and files it under Neo-Confucianism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Zhu Xi

Zhu Xi (1130–1200) was the Southern Song synthesizer of Neo-Confucianism whose commentaries on the Four Books became imperial orthodoxy for centuries. He organized cosmology of li (principle) and qi (vital stuff) and built academy pedagogy.

How to read this passage

Education is not only information transfer; it is the shaping of attention and character. Confucian learning, Socratic midwifery, and Deweyan growth offer rival models. This passage enters that discussion through learning.

Concepts in this quote

Learning
Learning is philosophy’s practical twin: how judgment is formed through study, error, dialogue, and habit.
